title: Almost Right
endLine: Counterfeits jam the nucleotide supply; cells dividing fastest are hit hardest.

scenes.tts: Last time, a cell recycled purines because building them is costly. A dividing cell must copy all its D N A, so it needs building blocks fast. One drug is shaped almost like the vitamin folate. How can a vitamin look-alike starve that copying?
scenes.narration: Last time, a cell recycled purines because building them is costly. A dividing cell must copy all its DNA, so it needs building blocks fast. One drug is shaped almost like the vitamin folate. How can a vitamin look-alike starve that copying?
scenes.caption: Last time, a cell recycled purines because building them is costly. A dividing cell must copy all its DNA, so it needs building blocks fast. One drug is shaped almost like the vitamin folate. How can a vitamin look-alike starve that copying?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's colour map without a reset. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, whole film: GREEN = a finished nucleotide (tokens and the pool); YELLOW = a free purine base; BLUE = an enzyme (chips); PURPLE = PRPP; ORANGE = ATP coins (recap only); RED = every block or 'broken' X; TEAL = a drug, now every counterfeit (as allopurinol was in the first film). New in this film: MAGENTA = the folate carrier (a plain ring icon, never a molecular structure); WHITE = DNA, drawn as a schematic ladder of two rails and rungs. THE WORLD, kept all film (16:9): at LEFT, the first film's round GREEN pool of nucleotide tokens with two doors on its rim, 'build' (PURPLE PRPP chip beside it) and 'recycle' (BLUE 'HGPRT' chip). At CENTRE, a BLUE gateway. At RIGHT, the WHITE DNA ladder fills about 65% of the frame height, with a copying fork sliding slowly down it and pulling in GREEN tokens. Below, a MAGENTA folate loop (built in s03 and s04). A small 'schematic' tag sits at bottom right throughout. During the link-back sentence, only the pool is lit: YELLOW bases drift out of it and most return through the BLUE recycle door; a few ORANGE coins hover by the build door, then fade. On 'dividing cell', the camera eases right to the WHITE ladder; the fork speeds up and GREEN tokens stream toward it. On 'shaped almost like the vitamin folate', a MAGENTA ring floats in, and beside it a TEAL ring of the same outline, labelled 'look-alike'. On the question, the stream of tokens to the fork thins and the fork slows. Large white text across the top: 'A fake vitamin stops copying?'

Title 'Almost Right' fades in above the world for 2 s while the question text fades out. The TEAL look-alike drifts off screen to wait. The fork resumes its normal pace; GREEN tokens keep flowing to it.

scenes.tts: But D N A needs deoxy building blocks. In a dividing cell, most new ones come through one gateway, ribonucleotide reductase, which reduces ribonucleotides. Its activity is tied tightly to cell division.
scenes.narration: But DNA needs deoxy building blocks. In a dividing cell, most new ones come through one gateway, ribonucleotide reductase, which reduces ribonucleotides. Its activity is tied tightly to cell division.
scenes.caption: But DNA needs deoxy building blocks. In a dividing cell, most new ones come through one gateway, ribonucleotide reductase, which reduces ribonucleotides. Its activity is tied tightly to cell division.
scenes.visual: The BLUE gateway at centre grows to a large arch labelled 'ribonucleotide reductase'. GREEN tokens leave the pool, pass through the arch and come out as GREEN-outlined tokens with a small 'd' tag (label once: 'deoxy'); these travel on to the fork. On 'most new ones', a thin side path into the deoxy stream appears faintly, unlabelled, to keep the hedge 'most'. On 'tied tightly to cell division', the fork and the arch pulse together: when the fork speeds up, more tokens pass the arch; when it slows, fewer do (schematic timing). Labels on screen: the arch, 'deoxy', the pool, the ladder.

scenes.tts: Thymine needs one more step. Thymidylate synthase adds a carbon, carried by a folate, to d U M P. That makes thymidylate, d T M P, and leaves the folate as dihydrofolate.
scenes.narration: Thymine needs one more step. Thymidylate synthase adds a carbon, carried by a folate, to dUMP. That makes thymidylate, dTMP, and leaves the folate as dihydrofolate.
scenes.caption: Thymine needs one more step. Thymidylate synthase adds a carbon, carried by a folate, to dUMP. That makes thymidylate, dTMP, and leaves the folate as dihydrofolate.
scenes.visual: Camera lowers so the folate loop fills the lower half; the pool, arch and ladder stay visible but dimmed above. A deoxy token labelled 'dUMP' drops from the arch to a BLUE chip 'thymidylate synthase' on the right side of the loop. A MAGENTA ring carrying a small bright MAGENTA dot (the carbon) arrives at the same chip. On 'adds a carbon', the dot hops from the ring onto the token, which relabels to 'dTMP' and rises to the fork; the fork takes it in as a rung. The ring, now without its dot, dims slightly and is labelled 'DHF'.

scenes.tts: Dihydrofolate reductase, D H F R, turns it back into T H F. Only then can it carry another carbon. The same carrier supplies two carbons of the purine ring. So one folate loop feeds both thymidylate and purines.
scenes.narration: Dihydrofolate reductase, DHFR, turns it back into THF. Only then can it carry another carbon. The same carrier supplies two carbons of the purine ring. So one folate loop feeds both thymidylate and purines.
scenes.caption: Dihydrofolate reductase, DHFR, turns it back into THF. Only then can it carry another carbon. The same carrier supplies two carbons of the purine ring. So one folate loop feeds both thymidylate and purines.
scenes.visual: The dimmed 'DHF' ring travels round the loop to a second BLUE chip on the left side, 'DHFR'. It brightens, relabels to 'THF' and picks up a fresh MAGENTA dot. The loop now turns continuously: THF to thymidylate synthase, DHF to DHFR, back to THF. On 'two carbons of the purine ring', a MAGENTA arrow grows from the THF side of the loop up to the PURPLE 'build' door of the pool, carrying two MAGENTA dots, labelled 'two ring carbons'. On 'feeds both', the dTMP path to the fork and the arrow to the build door pulse together. At most six labelled things: pool, build door, ladder, the two BLUE chips, THF/DHF ring.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. An enzyme accepts what has the right shape. A counterfeit that fits the lock well enough to turn it, or jam it, is a medicine, an antimetabolite. The dividing cell is the most exposed, because it needs nucleotides fastest.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. An enzyme accepts what has the right shape. A counterfeit that fits the lock well enough to turn it, or jam it, is a medicine, an antimetabolite. The dividing cell is the most exposed, because it needs nucleotides fastest.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule. An enzyme accepts what has the right shape. A counterfeit that fits the lock well enough to turn it, or jam it, is a medicine, an antimetabolite. The dividing cell is the most exposed, because it needs nucleotides fastest.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world, everything turning. The BLUE DHFR chip enlarges and shows a simple notch (a lock shape, not a molecular structure); the MAGENTA ring slots into it and slides on. The TEAL look-alike ring from s00 drifts back in, fits the same notch and STAYS; a RED stall mark flickers on the chip, then lifts as the TEAL ring drifts out again (preview only). Text at top: 'shape decides what fits'. On 'antimetabolite', the word appears in TEAL beneath the chip. On 'most exposed', the copying fork speeds up and its token stream thickens; a small 'fastest demand' tag appears on the fork.

scenes.tts: Methotrexate mimics folate and jams D H F R, the enzyme that recycles the carrier. What runs short: thymidylate, the purine ring, or both?
scenes.narration: Methotrexate mimics folate and jams DHFR, the enzyme that recycles the carrier. What runs short: thymidylate, the purine ring, or both?
scenes.caption: Methotrexate mimics folate and jams DHFR, the enzyme that recycles the carrier. What runs short: thymidylate, the purine ring, or both?
scenes.visual: The TEAL ring returns, labelled 'methotrexate', and lodges in the DHFR notch. A RED X appears on the DHFR chip and stays. The loop's motion slows but the outcome is NOT yet shown: the two outflows (dTMP to the fork, the MAGENTA arrow to the build door) are each marked with a white question mark. Question card at top in white: 'Thymidylate, purines, or both?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. The TEAL methotrexate ring sits in the DHFR notch under the RED X; DHF rings creep slowly toward the chip; the fork keeps moving gently. No other change.

scenes.tts: Both. With D H F R jammed, T H F is not regenerated. Thymidylate and the purine ring are both starved of their folate carbons. The cell runs short of the d T M P it needs to copy its D N A.
scenes.narration: Both. With DHFR jammed, THF is not regenerated. Thymidylate and the purine ring are both starved of their folate carbons. The cell runs short of the dTMP it needs to copy its DNA.
scenes.caption: Both. With DHFR jammed, THF is not regenerated. Thymidylate and the purine ring are both starved of their folate carbons. The cell runs short of the dTMP it needs to copy its DNA.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. DHF rings pile up beside the jammed DHFR chip; the THF side of the loop empties and no MAGENTA dots move. Both question marks turn into RED marks: the MAGENTA arrow to the build door fades to a dotted outline, and the dTMP path to the fork runs dry. On 'copy its DNA', the fork stops at a gap in the WHITE ladder where a 'T' rung is missing; tag 'no dTMP'.

scenes.tts: Five-fluorouracil mimics uracil. Inside the cell it becomes F d U M P, which traps thymidylate synthase itself. A different lock, the same shortage of d T M P.
scenes.narration: 5-fluorouracil mimics uracil. Inside the cell it becomes FdUMP, which traps thymidylate synthase itself. A different lock, the same shortage of dTMP.
scenes.caption: 5-fluorouracil mimics uracil. Inside the cell it becomes FdUMP, which traps thymidylate synthase itself. A different lock, the same shortage of dTMP.
scenes.visual: Reset the loop to running: the methotrexate ring and its RED X fade, MAGENTA dots move again, the fork restarts. A TEAL base token labelled '5-fluorouracil' enters, then gains the nucleotide outline of the dUMP token and relabels to 'FdUMP'. It lodges on the thymidylate synthase chip; a RED X appears there. Real dUMP tokens queue beside it; no dTMP leaves; the fork stops again at a missing 'T' rung. DHFR stays unblocked (no RED X there), and the THF arrow to the purine build door stays open.

scenes.tts: Six-mercaptopurine, a fake purine, enters through the recycle door. H G P R T, the recycling enzyme, turns it into counterfeit nucleotides. These shut down purine building. Once built into D N A, they damage the leukemia cells that took up the drug.
scenes.narration: 6-mercaptopurine, a fake purine, enters through the recycle door. HGPRT, the recycling enzyme, turns it into counterfeit nucleotides. These shut down purine building. Once built into DNA, they damage the leukemia cells that took up the drug.
scenes.caption: 6-mercaptopurine, a fake purine, enters through the recycle door. HGPRT, the recycling enzyme, turns it into counterfeit nucleotides. These shut down purine building. Once built into DNA, they damage the leukemia cells that took up the drug.
scenes.visual: The 5-FU block fades and the loop runs again. Camera shifts to the pool at left. A TEAL token shaped like the YELLOW bases, labelled '6-mercaptopurine', drifts in among real YELLOW bases. The BLUE HGPRT chip at the recycle door accepts it (the lock turns) and it enters the pool as a TEAL-outlined nucleotide token labelled 'counterfeit'. On 'shut down purine building', a RED bar closes across the PURPLE build door. On 'built into DNA', a counterfeit token travels through the arch to the fork and becomes a TEAL rung in the WHITE ladder; that stretch of ladder shows a RED crack. Tag on the ladder: 'leukemia cell'.

scenes.tts: So each of these drugs is almost right. Each fools an enzyme on the road to D N A. A dividing cell needs that road most, though fast-dividing normal tissues are hit too.
scenes.narration: So each of these drugs is almost right. Each fools an enzyme on the road to DNA. A dividing cell needs that road most, though fast-dividing normal tissues are hit too.
scenes.caption: So each of these drugs is almost right. Each fools an enzyme on the road to DNA. A dividing cell needs that road most, though fast-dividing normal tissues are hit too.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world, all running and unblocked. On 'almost right', three small TEAL ghosts appear at their locks in turn, each next to its BLUE chip: at DHFR, at thymidylate synthase, at the HGPRT recycle door. On 'the road to DNA', a white path lights from the pool through the arch to the fork. On 'needs that road most', the fork speeds up and its stream thickens. On 'normal tissues', a second, smaller WHITE ladder with a moving fork appears at the far right, labelled 'normal dividing tissue', its stream also thinning slightly when a TEAL ghost flickers.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (GREEN tokens flowing through the arch, the MAGENTA folate loop turning, the fork copying). Large white text, centred: 'Counterfeits jam the nucleotide supply; cells dividing fastest are hit hardest.'
